findings.claim: SVG payloads are materialized without an explicit full-payload size limit across inline, plain file, and themed file protocol paths.
findings.upstream_failure: At the pinned upstream head, TryCreatePlainSvg converts inline payloads with Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes and reads plain SVG files with File.ReadAllBytes; themed file loading reaches SvgFileTextReader.TryRead, which decodes the stream with ReadToEnd before TryCreateThemedSvg re-encodes the resolved template.
findings.counterevidence: The current upstream head already documents file-backed reads as icon-loader worker work, so the previous synchronous-STA claim no longer survives. SvgFileTextReader also bounds only the XML declaration probe and has BOM-less encoding coverage, so the previous encoding claim is no longer publishable. Those fixes do not impose a maximum on the complete SVG payload before allocation/parsing.
findings.why_not_already_fixed: The only explicit bound found is MaximumXmlDeclarationByteCount for the declaration probe; there is no size limit checked before Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes, File.ReadAllBytes, or StreamReader.ReadToEnd materialize the full SVG payload.
findings.verification: Exact upstream CmdPal unit-test project build passed in x64 Debug, and focused SVG protocol tests passed 13/13. This validates the remapped current behavior and confirms existing BOM/XML-encoding coverage, but it is not a stress reproduction of an oversized payload; the finding is grounded in the unbounded materialization paths.
